analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md, adding a 'Provider authorization guidance' section at head lines 77-87. It documents running ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests (swift test --skip-build --no-parallel --filter ...) from provider-swift/. The text says the suite uses fixed snapshots and injected process identity, and covers freshness checks, the receipt-window boundary, disabled rollout, missing or mismatched decisions and exact lease expiry. It states that it does not run host probes, change profiles or establish native App Attest acceptance. The section is documentation only, with no code, config, key handling, endpoint or workflow changes. It is consistent with the threat model's TB-011, T-053, T-057 and the platform-owned authorization language; it makes no production qualification claim and does not overclaim runtime secrecy (T-056). The command is a local test invocation with no secrets, no live provider state and no network. The remainder of the file (units 8 and 9) is unchanged context. It includes SSD test-volume guidance, which stays consistent with the T-041 cache posture (isolated keys, never production roots). No new attack surface, invalidated assumptions or threat-model gaps were identified. One unverified contract remains: whether ProviderAuthorizationReadinessTests exists and behaves as described. That is outside the supplied evidence and is a documentation-accuracy matter, not a security regression.
